kind: assumed inputs, analysis choices and cited scales; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository

rounding.note: A criterion (AIC, BIC) is computed from the log-likelihood already rounded to 3 decimals, and a difference from the rounded criteria, so that every figure can be recomputed by hand from the figures stored next to it.

candidates.note: Three distributions for the number of events in one day. Each treats the days as independent draws from one distribution: none has a parameter for the order of the days.

models.name: negative binomial
models.log_likelihood: sum over days of [ln(r) + ln(r + 1) + ... + ln(r + x - 1)] - sum(ln(x!)) + n r ln(r / (r + mu)) + sum(x) ln(mu / (r + mu))
models.maximum: mu = mean (closed form); r by a one-parameter search (r = 1 is the geometric, r -> infinity the Poisson)

search.note: The negative binomial's r is the zero of the score d(log L)/dr = sum over j of (days with a count above j) / (r + j) - n ln(1 + mean / r), found by bisection on the geometric mean of a bracket. A sample whose variance (divisor n) does not exceed its mean has no finite zero: its fit is the Poisson limit. A sample whose score is still positive at the upper bound is fitted at that bound.

golden_section.note: An independent check: a golden-section search that maximises the log-likelihood itself, used on all three models from three starting intervals each. It never produces a result of the lesson.

limit_checks.poisson_gap_formula: log L(negative binomial at r) - log L(Poisson) ~ n (variance with divisor n - mean) / (2 r) for large r

not_overdispersed_case.expected: variance 0.5 does not exceed the mean 3, so the negative binomial fit is the Poisson limit

sensitivity.note: An analysis choice, not an observation: refit the three candidates after leaving out the k busiest days. 4 is the number of days that hold 286 of the 594 events (the four busiest days of the syllabus); 11 is every day with 12 events or more.

deleted_triggers.note: Borrowed, not measured by this fixture: twelve trigger files were deleted without being archived, seven dated 2026-03-20 and five dated 2026-06-30 (PSY-009 reads them from the repository history; 'git log --diff-filter=D --name-only' at the pinned commit lists them). They are added to those two days to see whether the survivor set moves the ranking.

recovery.note: Seeded check. Each fitted model in turn generates samples of independent days; all three models are refitted to every sample and each criterion picks one. A sample is drawn by inverting the cumulative distribution with random.Random(seed * 1000 + days).random().

sticky_geometric.note: An assumed process, not a model of the project: each day repeats the previous day's count with the copy probability and is otherwise a fresh draw from the fitted geometric. Every day then has exactly the geometric distribution, and the lag-1 autocorrelation of the process equals the copy probability. It isolates the one assumption the three candidates share.
sticky_geometric.copy_probability_rule: the lag-1 autocorrelation of the observed daily counts, rounded to 2 decimals

cited_scales.note: Quoted from the two sources, which were read for this module. Neither scale is a probability that a model is true.

aic_difference.source: Burnham and Anderson (2004), 'Multimodel Inference: Understanding AIC and BIC in Model Selection', Sociological Methods & Research 33(2), p. 271
aic_difference.quantity: Delta_i = AIC_i - AIC_min, for a model i of the candidate set
aic_difference.between_bands: between the bands the source names
aic_difference.what_the_source_says: It calls these 'simple rules of thumb' and 'rough guidelines'; Delta_i measures how plausible it is that fitted model i is 'the best approximating model in the candidate set'. On p. 279, discussing BIC, it adds that observing a posterior model probability p_t near 1 'does not justify an inference that model g_t is truth (such a statistical inference requires an a priori certainty that the true model is in the model set)'.

twice_log_bayes_factor.source: Kass and Raftery (1995), 'Bayes Factors', Journal of the American Statistical Association 90(430), p. 777
twice_log_bayes_factor.quantity: 2 ln(B10), the Bayes factor for hypothesis 1 against hypothesis 0; a BIC difference is a rough approximation to it (p. 778)

bands.label: not worth more than a bare mention

twice_log_bayes_factor.between_bands: not applicable: the bands are contiguous
twice_log_bayes_factor.what_the_source_says: 'these categories are not a calibration of the Bayes factor, but rather a rough descriptive statement about standards of evidence in scientific investigation' (p. 777). The Schwarz criterion 'may be viewed as a rough approximation to the logarithm of the Bayes factor'; minus twice it 'is often called the Bayesian information criterion (BIC)'; 'the relative error of exp(S) in approximating B12 is generally O(1)' (p. 778).

hypothesis_thresholds.note: The hypothesis of the research cycle was written before the fixture ran. These thresholds make its parts checkable; the two 'within' tolerances and the 1% share were fixed after the fits and the autocorrelation had been seen in an exploratory run, but before the seeded check ran.

bic_picks_negative_binomial_when_geometr.expected: P(chi-square with 1 degree of freedom > ln(days))

exercise_3.note: An imaginary two-week log, not project data: BIC is assumed to be lower for the geometric than for the negative binomial by the stated difference. The two shares come from the seeded check at that length.

transfer_task.note: A hypothetical help desk, not Streeling data: tickets opened per day over 14 consecutive days.

worked_by_hand.note: The mean is 28 / 14 = 2, so every deviation is a whole number and the two sums can be done on paper.
